title: What Is This? Scenario and Review
summary: Use sa a and sa yo to point out singular and plural things, then combine demonstratives with ownership.

sketchBlocks.title: sa a — this / that
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Use **sa a** after a noun to point out one thing:

- **valiz sa a** — this/that bag
- **machin sa a** — this/that car

The demonstrative follows the noun.

tryItExercises.title: Build “this book”
tryItExercises.prompt: Arrange the Kreyòl phrase for “this book.”
tryItExercises.hint: Put sa a after the noun.

help.hint_1: Use the Kreyòl pattern from this lesson.
help.hint_2: Use the pattern you just learned.

sketchBlocks.title: sa yo — these / those
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
For more than one thing, use **sa yo**:

- **kaye sa yo** — these/those notebooks
- **liv sa yo** — these/those books

The final **yo** marks the plural.

tryItExercises.title: Build “these cars”
tryItExercises.prompt: Arrange the Kreyòl phrase for “these cars.”
tryItExercises.hint: Put sa yo after the noun.

help.hint_1: Use the Kreyòl pattern from this lesson.
help.hint_2: Use the pattern you just learned.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Point and Say Who Owns It
sketchBlocks.title: Valiz sa a se pou Mari
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Combine the demonstrative with **se pou**:

- **Valiz sa a se pou Mari.** — This/that bag is Mari's.
- **Kaye sa yo se pou nou.** — These/those notebooks are ours.

This is a practical way to talk about objects around you.

tryItExercises.prompt: Arrange the Kreyòl sentence for “This car is Jan’s.”
tryItExercises.hint: Use noun + sa a + se pou + person.
